title: Adaptive telemetry ingest filter and schema validation service
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: The Console emits a high-volume mix of usage events (route hits, token usage, rollout decisions) that flow into the central analytics pipeline. Currently we accept events with a permissive schema which has led to downstream parsing errors, duplicated joins, and increased storage costs. Problem: intermittent schema drift from client SDKs and delayed validation causes noisy metrics, delayed alerting, and production ingestion backpressure. Goal: Implement an adaptive ingest filter service colocated with the Console backend that validates and normalizes incoming telemetry against an evolving schema registry, applies lightweight transformations (field renames, unit normalization), and rejects or routes invalid events to a quarantine topic for offline inspection. The service should be low-latency (<5ms added p99), horizontally scalable, and support schema evolution semantics (additive fields allowed, typed migrations, version pinning per customer).
acceptance_criteria: Ingest filter rejects events that fail mandatory field checks and emits a rejection metric with reasons
Validated events are published to analytics-kafka.v1 with schema version header set
Invalid events are written to analytics-quarantine topic with original payload and validation errors
End-to-end p99 added latency for validation < 5ms under steady-state load (validated via load test)
Regression tests covering 5 schema-evolution scenarios included in CI
Dashboard showing validation rates, rejection reasons, and consumer lag is available in Grafana
tech_notes: Schema registry: use protobuf-first registry hosted at internal-schema.redwood (proto files stored in git with tags)
Validation library: extend existing streaming-schema-gatekeeper primitives (ENG-6172) to support adaptive rules and normalization hooks
Backpressure strategy: when downstream lag exceeds 5 minutes, apply sampling and emit a throttled-metric; do not return 5xx to console clients—use graceful drop with detailed metrics
API contract: synchronous validation on write path; fallback option to accept-then-validate asynchronously controlled by per-customer config (default synchronous)
Observability: add metrics for validated_count, rejected_count_by_reason, validation_latency_ms histogram, quarantine_topic_size
Security: scrubPII hook to remove or hash user identifiers before writing to quarantine; integrate with current KMS for encryption at rest
migration_steps: 1) Deploy validation service in a canary region with feature flag off
2) Mirror 1% of incoming traffic through a tap to the validator and write validated events to a test topic
3) Run end-to-end consumer tests against test topic and compare metrics to baseline
4) Gradually increase mirror rate (1 -> 10 -> 50%) while monitoring rejection rates and latency
5) Enable synchronous validation for non-critical routes, keep heavy routes on accept-then-validate until optimizations complete
6) Backfill quarantine topic processing pipeline and triage tooling
7) Flip feature flag cluster-wide and deprecate legacy permissive ingest path after 2 weeks of stable metrics
